name: Block abilities
summary: A hit, a mark, a pulse or an aura stops enemies from using their abilities for a few seconds: their keys lock, channels they run are cut off, toggles are switched off or frozen as they are, and in some versions passive effects such as stealth, regeneration or auras switch off too. They can still move and fire their weapons, which sets it apart from the weapon trait silence (no firing either), from stun (nothing at all) and from disable-machine (machines only). Its value lies in timing: block an escape, a shield or a heal just before the team strikes, or keep a caster from supporting its allies. Versions differ in what they cover (keys only, passives as well, the victim's deployed devices) and in how they land (a weapon's hits, a thrown device, a held link, an area, every marked target).
counterplay: Stay out of reach: most blocks need a hit, a short link or a set radius (Sombra's hack in Overwatch works only at short range), so keep your distance or break line of sight.
Shoot the device or the caster: Valorant's ZERO/point knife can be destroyed during its wind-up, and damage interrupts Sombra's hack.
Cleanse or dispel it: some Overwatch abilities remove the hacked state, and in Warcraft III a dispel or an anti-magic shell cast by a unit outside the silenced area answers the Dark Ranger's Silence.
Keep fighting with your gun: weapons still work, so a unit that leans on its weapon loses little; save your abilities until the block fades.
Act first: effects already cast keep running in Dota 2, and in Valorant a scouting gadget already sent off carries on, so use the key ability before the block lands.
Deny the trigger: when the block rides on a mark (Tempest Rising's EM Interference), avoiding or outlasting the marking fire avoids the block too.
Spread out against area blocks, and expect heroes to shake them off sooner (Warcraft III's silence lasts half as long on heroes).

other_examples.unit: HAYWIRE missiles (Scrambler, Haywire Turret) and other sources of Silence
other_examples.note: The Scrambler's missiles, like the Haywire Turret's, mark and silence what they hit. In this game a silenced unit cannot use its active or passive abilities, and the pages never say it stops attacking. Vehicles pushed into Tempest Overflow are silenced as well, and the EM Interference doctrine silences every Marked enemy; it names the Sentinel, Comms Officer, Drone Command Unit, Support Beacon and Marking Mine as the markers.

sources.title: Doctrine, Tempest Rising Wiki
sources.note: EM Interference, fifth step of the GDF Comms tree, with the markers it lists.

other_examples.note: A targeted area spell: every enemy inside cannot cast spells for a while, heroes for half as long, and higher levels widen the area and lengthen the effect. The wiki calls her generally the only unit that can keep enemy spellcasters from supporting their allies; a dispel or an anti-magic shell from a unit outside the area answers it.

sources.title: Dark Ranger, Liquipedia Warcraft III Wiki

other_examples.note: In this top-down hero game, silence stops a unit's active abilities but not its items: channels end at once, toggles stay stuck as they are, and effects already cast keep going. Passives keep working; a separate status, break, turns those off, and another, mute, locks items. As a lighter disable than a stun, a silence usually lasts longer, and players use it to keep a hero from blinking or vanishing during a gank and to stop spells being combined in a teamfight.

shooter_analogues.note: Sombra holds secondary fire on an enemy within short range, keeping line of sight through a brief wind-up. A hacked hero cannot use any of its abilities, ultimates and movement passives included, for a short moment and stays revealed to her team for longer, while it still moves and fires its weapons normally. Taking damage interrupts the hack and puts it on a short cooldown; it also works on health packs and on devices such as turrets. A few allied abilities cleanse it, and being unstoppable prevents the lock.

sources.title: Status effect, Overwatch Wiki
sources.note: The Hacked section says hacked heroes keep their weapons and normal movement.

shooter_analogues.note: KAY/O throws a knife that sticks where it lands and winds up for a moment, during which enemies can shoot it apart; then it pulses through walls and suppresses every enemy agent in range for several seconds, and his team learns who was hit, though not exactly where. A suppressed agent cannot cast or ready abilities, loses control of guided ones and cannot trigger follow-up activations; the traps and turrets a suppressed Sentinel agent has placed shut down as if their owner had died, while scouting gadgets already sent off keep working.

Before his rework, Revenant's tactical threw a device that hurt enemies and switched off their abilities for a time. Patches made it cancel a grapple already under way and a phase attempt, and stop cloaked and combat revives; the rework later took it away from him.

sources.title: Revenant, Apex Legends Wiki
sources.note: Patch history and the box of his original abilities.

player_translation.summary: A short window in which the enemy's abilities go grey while their guns keep working. The user times it for just before the team strikes, so escapes, shields and heals fail when they matter; the victims keep fighting with their weapons and wait it out or get cleansed.
as_user: Apply the block by the variant's means: a weapon hit, a thrown pulse, a short held link, an area, or, with the mark-linked variant, every enemy your team has marked.

Blocked enemies cannot use their ability keys for a few seconds, channels and toggles they are running stop, and with the passive-breaking versions their cloaks, regeneration and auras switch off; they can still move and shoot.
Aim it at the enemy about to escape, shield up or heal, or at the support whose boosts hold their push together, and let your team finish the job.
The block itself does no damage; your weapon is ordinary, so the window is only worth what you and your teammates do with it.
as_target: Your ability icons grey out with a lock and a countdown; your weapons and movement still work.
Fight with your gun, step out of the area or behind cover, and wait it out; a teammate's cleanse ends it early.
Watch for the tell (a device winding up, a link beam, an aura's edge) and use your key ability first, or shoot the device.
teammates: The blocker sets up and the damage dealers finish: a setup-finisher pair.
The victims' team carries cleanses or immunity effects to lift the block, and spreads out against area versions.
An ability-heavy team needs someone to hunt the blocker or stay out of its reach.
controls: Pulse variant: Q throws a device that sticks and pulses after a short wind-up; enemies can shoot it first. One counted key.
Hack variant: hold right mouse on an enemy at short range through a short wind-up; damage to you interrupts it.
On-hit and mark-linked variants: no key; your weapon's hits or your team's marks apply it.
Victims need no key: their ability keys simply do nothing until it ends.
feedback: Blocked units carry a lock or static icon that both teams see, and their own HUD greys the ability icons with a countdown.
A sharp electronic crackle when the block lands and a short chime when it ends.
A thrown device shows its radius during the wind-up, and a held link draws a beam.
Passives that switch off do so visibly: a cloaked unit flickers into view, an aura's ring disappears.
changes_from_rts: In Tempest Rising the doctrine silences every Marked enemy for as long as the mark lasts. On a player a long block feels like losing half the unit, so the player version lasts a few seconds and is followed by a short immunity.
RTS units have one or two buttons; a player unit's abilities are its identity, so the block must never touch weapons or movement, and it must be obvious on screen.
RTS silence rides on automatic fire with no warning; here the active versions get a visible wind-up or a device that can be shot.
In the RTS, blocking marked targets comes free once the doctrine is bought, because marking is cheap; here the mark-linked version is a high-tier variant.

team_play.notes: The block is worth what the team does inside the window, so it pairs a blocker with damage dealers. Ability-heavy enemies must answer it with spacing, cleanses or someone who hunts the blocker.

notes: A status flag that every ability checks before it fires, and that passives check while they run.
Each ability needs a rule for what the block does to it while it is running: cut it, freeze it or leave it alone.
World and HUD icons, cleanse interactions, and a short immunity after a block ends to stop chain-blocking.
Blocking escapes and defensive abilities sets up near-certain kills, so keep it short, telegraphed and followed by immunity.
Against units built around their abilities it can feel like losing the unit; signature abilities could resist it, as Warcraft III heroes shake off silence twice as fast.
Mark-linked blocking from cheap marking weapons can lock out a whole team at once; keep it at a high tier or give it a cost.
A lock icon and greyed keys read easily; the risk is a pile of overlapping status icons in big fights.

variants.name: Block on hit
variants.summary: Your weapon's hits block the target's abilities for a moment.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Scrambler and Haywire Turret (HAYWIRE missiles)

variants.name: Block pulse
variants.summary: A thrown device sticks where it lands and, after a short wind-up during which it can be shot, pulses through walls and blocks every enemy in range; your team learns who was hit.
variants.seen_in: Valorant KAY/O's ZERO/point; Apex Legends Revenant's original Silence

variants.name: Hack link
variants.summary: Hold on one enemy at short range through a short wind-up to lock its abilities briefly and reveal it to your team for longer; damage interrupts you, and the same link shuts down enemy devices such as turrets.

variants.name: Area silence
variants.summary: Target an area: every enemy in it loses its abilities for a while, elite units and heroes for half as long.

variants.name: Block the marked
variants.summary: Every enemy your team has marked is also blocked for as long as the mark lasts.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising EM Interference doctrine (Sentinel, Comms Officer, Drone Command Unit, Marking Mine)

variants.name: Break passives
variants.summary: Switch off only passive abilities (auras, regeneration, stealth, on-hit effects) for a time, while ability keys still work.

adds_strengths.why: Shuts off enemy escapes, shields and heals for a few seconds so the team can finish the target.

adds_weaknesses.why: Leaves enemy weapons alone, so a target with a strong gun still fights back, and units with few abilities lose little.

counters.why: Units that escape with a dash, leap or teleport are stuck in the fight while blocked, which is how Dota 2 players use silence in a gank.
Shields, invulnerability and self-heals on a key cannot be used while blocked.
Healers and casters who keep their team going cannot cast, which is how Warcraft III players use silence on spellcasters.

countered_by.why: Most blocks reach only a short distance or a set radius, so long-range units hit the blocker from outside it.
Phasing out or turning immune sheds the block or keeps it from landing, as in Overwatch.

open_questions: Should the block switch off passive abilities too, as Tempest Rising's silence does, or only keys, as Dota 2's silence does (with a separate break for passives)?
How long may a block last on a player? Overwatch's hack locks a hero's abilities for only about a second; the proposal here is a few seconds with a short immunity afterwards.
Should signature abilities resist the block (a shorter lock), as Warcraft III heroes resist silence?

Word lists: the weapon trait silence says the target can neither fire nor use abilities, but its coding rule asks for it when a weapon stops firing or abilities, so an ability-only block on a weapon (Tempest Rising's HAYWIRE missiles) would be coded as silence today. A later word-list version could narrow the rule and send ability-only blocks to this pattern.
Tempest Rising's pages never say whether a silenced unit can still attack; this pattern reads the silence as ability-only, which the Sentinel's own entry also notes as uncertain.

shooter_fit.reason: Hero shooters already use it: Overwatch's hack, Valorant's suppression and Apex Legends' old Silence all lock abilities while guns keep working, and a lock icon reads well from above. It frustrates if it lasts long, so it must stay short and well telegraphed.
